text: Writing clean code is a skill that every programmer should develop. It is not just about making the computer understand your instructions, but also about making the code easy for other humans to read. The most important rule is to write code that is clear and straightforward. This starts with using good naming conventions. Variable and function names should be descriptive, such as "calculateTotalPrice" instead of "calc" or "x". This way, anyone reading the code knows what it does without needing extra comments. Another key idea is to keep your functions short and focused. Each function should do one simple thing. This makes your code more maintainable, as fixing a bug or adding a new feature becomes much easier when the logic is broken into small, logical pieces.
